x: Bob Rickitts, the writer, Harry, Charlie Wells, Alec. Spendlove, Wil Hawker and Harry Hanger were a strong level seven, and during the next two winter seasons the club won almost every open team race at both distances.

These seven were Jimmy Belchamber, Harry Evans, Harry Hanger, Bill Hawker, Bob Ricketts, Alec Spendlove and Charlie Wells. Amongst these Harry was at a disadvantage in respect of age, but he was in our scoring four many times.
Only one U.K. competitor was ahead of him, Tim Bonsor 3rd in 10.74, with the first two positions going to the Americans Edwards, 10.48 and Charlie Wells, 10.65.

The Rotary Watches International Games saw one of the best 100 metre line-ups seen in the United Kingdom: Silvio Leonard (Cuba) - the world's fastest in 1977 with an incredible 9.98, Osvaldo Lara (Cuba) - a best of 10.11, Charlie Wells (USA), Allan Wells, Haseley Crawford and Ernest Obeng.
